Answer: F
Reason: The chest radiograph shows dextrocardia (situs inversus) with the gastric bubble on the right and heart apex pointing right. In Kartagener's syndrome with situs inversus, bronchiectasis typically affects the morphologic lower lobes, which are located on the patient's left side due to the mirror-image anatomy; the image demonstrates more pronounced reticular/bronchiectatic changes in the left lung field compared to the right.
